S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: A persistent perception that one is useless or inferior to others.
subtypes.Self-Criticism: Excessively and repeatedly blaming oneself for past minor failures or flaws.
subtypes.Reduced Self-Efficacy: Distrust in one's own ability to perform tasks or solve problems.
subtypes.Chronic Sense of Inferiority: Persistently evaluating oneself lower in comparison to others.
subtypes.Lack of Self-Assurance: Continually feeling anxious and unsure about decisions or actions.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a depressed mood lasting for at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional depressive features that cause clinically significant distress or functional impairment. It typically presents with a long-standing pattern of low mood, low energy, poor self-esteem, and cognitive or sleep changes that are less severe than major depressive episodes but more enduring. The course is often insidious, beginning in response to psychosocial stressors or temperament vulnerabilities and then becoming a persistent baseline state, sometimes punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes (“double depression”). It is distinguished from Major Depressive Disorder primarily by its chronicity and often earlier, more gradual onset, and from normal sadness by its persistence, pervasiveness, and impact on functioning and quality of life.

patient.personality: He is meticulous and structured with a quiet competitive streak, enjoying being dependable in his work and active in community and church activities while remaining somewhat skeptical of new ideas.
patient.stressor: About four years ago, Geno’s company underwent a major restructuring that automated portions of the data entry process and shifted many of his long-time colleagues to other departments or locations, leaving him in a smaller, more isolated role with fewer opportunities for advancement. Around the same time, his children became more independent and one left home for college, altering his daily routines and reducing the sense of being needed that he had derived from both work and family life. Over the next three years, his days became increasingly repetitive, with long stretches of solitary computer work, canceled pickup games due to others’ schedules, and fewer social gatherings, which contrasted sharply with his earlier sense of camaraderie at the office and in the community. As he noticed a persistent, unshakable heaviness that colored his enjoyment of church choir, volunteering, and even his beloved weekend barbecues, and his spouse observed that he seemed down most of the time, he eventually agreed to see a psychiatrist because he felt stuck in a low mood that he could not shake on his own.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve just felt down and heavy for years now, like I can’t shake this low mood no matter what I do.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days it just feels like there’s this gray film over everything—church, work, even family dinners—like I’m going through the motions but there’s this steady heaviness in my chest that never really lifts, no matter what I do.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I go to bed tired enough, but I’ll lie there for an hour or more with my mind chewing on little things from work, and then I’m up two or three times in the night and wake up before my alarm feeling like I haven’t really rested.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: At work now I catch myself rereading the same line of numbers a few times because my mind drifts off, and even simple things like deciding which bill to pay first or what to make for dinner feel like they take way more mental effort than they used to.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.
S042.manifestation: Somewhere along the way I started thinking of myself as just a guy who types numbers and takes up space, and when someone at church or at home compliments me, my first reaction is to brush it off because I feel like they’re just being nice and I don’t really measure up.
